item.title: Iryna Zarutska stabbing case: Trump calls killing of Ukrainian woman 'horrific'
item.description: Donald Trump condemned the murder of Iryna Zarutska, a Ukrainian refugee, in Charlotte, North Carolina, blaming lenient bail laws for the tragedy. He described the suspect, Decarlos Brown, as a "career criminal" with a history of arrests and releases on cashless bail. Trump linked the case to his broader argument against cashless bail policies, highlighting the need to lock up dangerous criminals to protect innocent lives.

item.title: A curvy sketch, a secretive line: What's in the alleged Donald Trump's letter to Epstein?
item.description: House Democrats released a sexually suggestive letter, purportedly from Donald Trump to Jeffrey Epstein in 2003, reigniting scrutiny of their past ties. Trump denies authoring the note and drawing, dismissing it as false. The release coincides with congressional pressure for transparency on Epstein-related documents, as lawmakers seek further investigation into the matter.

item.title: Israel's final warning to Hamas: 'Mighty hurricane' to hit Gaza
item.description: Israel issued a final warning to Gaza City residents, urging them to evacuate immediately ahead of intensified airstrikes and ground operations if Hamas fails to release hostages and disarm. Prime Minister Netanyahu declared an impending "ground operation" after demolishing 50 "terror towers.

item.title: Court upholds writer's $83.3 million defamation ruling against Trump
SC backs Trump on aggressive immigration raids in California
item.description: The Supreme Court has sided with the Trump administration, allowing federal agents to conduct immigration raids in Southern California. This decision puts on hold a lower court's order that restricted agents from detaining individuals based on race, ethnicity, or language. The court's liberal justices dissented, with Justice Sotomayor expressing concern over potential targeting of Latinos.

item.title: Spain bans Israel-bound weapons ships, planes; Tel Aviv calls move anti-semitic
item.description: Spain has banned ships and aircraft carrying weapons to Israel from using its ports and airspace due to the Gaza offensive. This move, denounced by Israel as anti-Semitic, prompted Spain to recall its ambassador. Additionally, Spain will bar entry to individuals involved in "genocide" in Gaza, a claim Israel denies.

item.title: In a first, South Korean women target US military in suit over prostitution
item.description: Dozens of South Korean women, formerly prostitutes, are suing the US military, alleging decades of sex trade promotion and forced STD treatment. They accuse the military of managing a prostitution network around its bases, echoing a prior court victory against the South Korean government for encouraging this trade to benefit the economy.
item.dc:creator: Choe Sang Hun

item.title: Bangladesh's Jamaat wants hiring of music teachers scrapped
item.description: Bangladesh's Jamaat-e-Islami (JeI) has criticized the government's decision to recruit music and dance teachers in primary schools. JeI Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar termed the move "regrettable and irrational," advocating instead for the appointment of religious teachers.

item.title: No fairs around Durga Puja mandaps in Bangladesh; home adviser links them with cannabis, alcohol
item.description: In Bangladesh, fairs near Durga Puja mandaps are prohibited this year to curb anti-social activities like drug consumption. While a few shops may be allowed with permission, around 33,000 puja mandaps are expected nationwide. A mobile application has been developed to enhance security during the peaceful celebrations.

item.title: France to get 5th PM in less than 2 years as parliament votes to oust Francois Bayrou
item.description: In a major political upheaval, the French government collapsed after losing a confidence vote over its debt reduction plans. Prime Minister Francois Bayrou will resign, leaving President Macron to appoint a new leader amid growing financial market concerns. Opposition parties rejected Bayrou's austerity measures, leading to his downfall.

item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged Gaza City residents to evacuate as troops prepare for an intensified ground operation, following deadly attacks in Jerusalem where two Palestinian gunmen killed six.
